title: Global Climate Justice from the South
description: This online course examines the science, policy, and politics of global climate change with an emphasis on the Global South, and a social science focus on equity and justice. Students will learn directly from expert faculty from across the UC system and beyond. In addition, students will engage with readings and multimedia content to deepen their understanding of the most pressing climate change issues and solutions. Students will be evaluated through a variety of written products (review questions, journal responses, and a final paper) in which they identify connections across seemingly disparate places. Students will gain knowledge and skills needed to identify the larger system changes needed to adequately address the climate crisis.

title: Theories of Peace, Conflict and Violence
description: Fundamental issues relating to global peace and security: Focus on "negative peace"--the problem of war and organized violence; peace as the avoidance of war.

title: World Society in Transformation: Building Enduring Peace
description: Fundamental exploration of issues relating to global peace and security with a focus on "positive peace"--peace as human rights, sustainable development, ecological balance, political participation and other positive aspects of human security.

title: Theory and Practice of Nonviolence
description: Critical examination of nonviolence as a philosophy of life and as a pragmatic approach to conflict resolution. Philosophical, psychological, cultural, and political aspects. Major theorists of nonviolence including Gandhi, King, Dharp. Application to confict at all levels: interpersonal, intergroup, and international. Case studies.

title: Group Studies for Global Peace and Security
description: Intensive analysis of topics and themes in global peace and security. Topics will vary with instructor and year.

title: Global Peace and Security Seminar
description: Intensive analysis of methods and problems of global peace and security. Topics will vary with the instructor and quarter.

title: Pillars of Teaching Assistantship
description: “Pillars of Teaching Assistantship” course provides Teaching Assistants (TAs) with a comprehensive, research-based foundation for their teaching roles. The course includes an introductory session on common TA challenges, six interactive classes based on the four Pillars of Teaching Assistantship, and two community-focused classes on navigating challenges and setting boundaries. Additionally, a concluding session will recap the course content and prepare TAs for their future pedagogical careers at UCSB and beyond.

title: College and University Teaching-From Theory to Practice
description: Graduate students who are interested in a career in college and university teaching will gain experience in applying pedagogical theories and evidence-based teaching into course design, implementation, assessment and evaluation.

title: Introduction to Graduate Writing Expectations
description: Graduate students who would like to develop their writing skills will have the opportunity to practice drafting and revising a variety of advanced writing assignments common to the graduate experience. Students will first study the rhetorical features associated with various advanced graduate writing genres before producing disciplinary-specific versions of these texts.
prerequisites_raw: Graduate students must have completed no more than one year of course work to enroll. Should students attempt to enroll in any section of this course other than GRAD/WRIT 280AA, students must ensure that their disciplinary field is included in that special topic of the course.

title: Introduction to Article Writing
description: Graduate students interested in learning the underlying conventions related to professional academic writing through article writing will have the opportunity to draft and revise a disciplinary-relevant article. Students will first study the rhetorical features associated with articles, by discipline, in order to learn the conventions pertinent to article writing in students chosen fields. Then, students will produce a discipline- and journal-specific draft of an article.
prerequisites_raw: Graduate students must have completed the relevant research/scholarship to produce an article. Students who are still in the middle of their research projects will not be admitted. Should students attempt to enroll in any section of this course other than GRAD/WRIT 281AA, students must ensure that their disciplinary field is included in that special topic of the course.

title: Preparing for the Academic Job Market
description: Graduate students will have the job market process demystified while preparing a dossier of requested materials. Students will first study the rhetorical features associated with the major documents required for these positions and then produce discipline-specific drafts (with feedback provided).
prerequisites_raw: Students have to be, at the earliest, one year away from applying to the job market.
